Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

bssd 0.1.0

  • First version.
  • bdribs_post() computes the posterior distribution of the rate ratio under the BDRIBS model of Mukhopadhyay et al. (2018) as specified by Duncan (2026), with the total exposure time (BDRIBS(1)) or the total time at risk (BDRIBS(2)) as exposure. The background rate has a Gamma prior from historical placebo data (lambda_hp, pt_hp, df), or it is known when pt_hp = Inf (the screening analysis of Mukhopadhyay et al., 2018).
  • expbern_post() and llbern_post() compute the posterior distributions under the exponential Bernoulli (EXP_BERN) and the log-logistic Bernoulli (LL_BERN) mixture models of Duncan (2026) from subject-level data (y, t). For LL_BERN, the relative risk is the ratio of the cumulative incidences at t_star, and the priors of the study drug parameters can be set with mu_d_prior and sigma_d_prior.
  • All posterior quantities are computed by numerical integration instead of Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling. expbern_post() and llbern_post() repeat the computation on a finer grid and report an estimate of the integration error when control$check is TRUE (the default).
  • time_at_risk() computes the total exposure time and the total time at risk from subject-level data. ll_cdf() and ll_mu() give the cumulative incidence and the location parameter of the log-logistic distribution.
  • sim_blinded() simulates blinded trial data with exponential or log-logistic times to the event, and sim_oc() estimates the operating characteristics of the models by simulation.
  • print() and summary() methods for the results (class bssd_post).
  • The folder inst/reproduce reproduces the numerical results of Mukhopadhyay et al. (2018) and Duncan (2026), and inst/validation compares the package with the bdribs package, with MCMC in JAGS and with independent Python implementations.

Developed by Gosuke Homma.
